vulnerabilities.description: Protobuf varint decoder lacks bounds checking on array index. The varint parsing loop increments `i` without verifying bounds, risking buffer over-read with crafted messages.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Send malformed protobuf with high varint values causing i >= bytes.length, reading past buffer.
vulnerabilities.fix: Add bounds check: `if (i >= bytes.length) return null;` in varint loop

vulnerabilities.description: XML parser lacks recursion depth limits for entity expansion. Recursive entity definitions could cause stack overflow or DoS.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Craft ZWO with nested entity definitions triggering deep recursion in decodeEntities().
vulnerabilities.fix: Track recursion depth, enforce max_depth=10 limit in parseXml/decodeEntities

vulnerabilities.description: Scrypt parameters use n=2^14, below 2024 OWASP recommendations (2^16 minimum). Reduces KDF strength against brute-force.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Attacker can attempt password cracking with reduced computational cost due to lower KDF iterations.
vulnerabilities.fix: Update to n=2^16, r=8, p=1: `hashlib.scrypt(..., n=2**16, r=8, p=1)`

vulnerabilities.description: localStorage checkpoint serializes full ride records array every 60s without size validation. Quota exhaustion on 2+ hour rides.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Record 3-hour ride with high sample rate (1Hz), checkpoint triggers O(n) JSON.stringify every 60s, quota failure causes data loss.
vulnerabilities.fix: Implement ring-buffer strategy: keep only latest 2000 samples in localStorage checkpoint, full history in memory

vulnerabilities.description: Upload API tokens (intervals.icu API key, Strava bearer token) stored in sessionStorage with plaintext encoding. XSS in portal DOM can steal tokens.
vulnerabilities.exploit: DOM-based XSS in SVG rendering → access sessionStorage → steal intervals.icu/Strava API credentials → unauthorized activity upload.
vulnerabilities.fix: Move tokens to ephemeral in-memory Map, never persist to storage. Implement token refresh-on-init flow.

vulnerabilities.description: Basic auth encodes credentials with btoa() for intervals.icu. No HTTPS enforcement, credentials visible in plain HTTP if downgraded.
vulnerabilities.exploit: MITM on non-HTTPS connection intercepts btoa('API_KEY:key') header, steals intervals.icu API key.
vulnerabilities.fix: Enforce HTTPS via Content-Security-Policy, add warning if location.protocol !== 'https:', migrate to OAuth2

vulnerabilities.description: Pre-filled Garmin login form with email in DOM (if sessionStorage persists 'email' field). Visible to logged-in co-browser users.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Shared machine, second user opens paceforge portal, previous athlete's email visible in form field.
vulnerabilities.fix: Never pre-fill email in login form. Fetch from runner after login, not from sessionStorage.

vulnerabilities.description: FIT encoder uses Math.round() on power values without overflow guards. Max UINT32 = 4.3B watts (unrealistic but spec doesn't validate).
vulnerabilities.exploit: Hypothetical future power meter > 2^32W causes silent truncation in FIT file, misreported power in upload.
vulnerabilities.fix: Add assertion: `if (v > INVALID[type]) throw new Error('value overflow')`

vulnerabilities.description: SVG fill colors in profileShapes() are hardcoded from COGGAN_ZONES, but color injection vector exists if zone data becomes dynamic or user-controlled.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Future: if step.zone comes from untrusted source, attacker embeds JS via SVG fill attribute.
vulnerabilities.fix: Sanitize SVG attributes: validate hex colors with regex `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$`, reject anything else

vulnerabilities.description: GarminClient instantiation passes plaintext password parameter. Could appear in exception tracebacks or debug logs.
vulnerabilities.exploit: Unhandled exception in garmin_login_start() stack trace printed to logs includes password parameter in locals.
vulnerabilities.fix: Wrap password in custom class: `class Secret(str): def __repr__(self): return '***'`

riskScoreReasoning: High-severity buffer overflow in Zwift Ride protocol (exploitable with crafted device), weak scrypt KDF (offline password cracking), and XML DoS create significant risk. Medium-severity credential exposure and localStorage quota exhaustion pose realistic threats. Overall: 52/100 (moderate-to-high, defensible with listed fixes).

recommendations.title: Fix protobuf varint decoder bounds checking
recommendations.description: Enforce `i < bytes.length` guard in decodeControllerNotification() varint loop to prevent buffer over-read
recommendations.risk_mitigated: Buffer overflow / crash from untrusted device data

recommendations.title: Add XML entity recursion depth limits
recommendations.description: Track depth in parseXml/decodeEntities, enforce max 10 levels to prevent XXE amplification
recommendations.risk_mitigated: DoS via malformed ZWO workout files

recommendations.title: Upgrade scrypt KDF parameters
recommendations.description: Update n=2^16 (was 2^14) to meet 2024 standards. Regenerate login test hash.

recommendations.title: Implement ring-buffer for localStorage checkpoints
recommendations.description: Store only latest 2000 samples in checkpoint, keep full history in memory. Prevents quota exhaustion on long rides.
recommendations.risk_mitigated: Data loss on 2+ hour rides due to storage quota

recommendations.title: Move API credentials from sessionStorage to ephemeral memory
recommendations.description: Store intervals.icu/Strava tokens in-memory Map, not sessionStorage. Prompt for re-entry on tab reload.
recommendations.risk_mitigated: Token theft via XSS / DOM inspection

recommendations.title: Enforce HTTPS for sensitive requests
recommendations.description: Add CSP header blocking http:, warn user if upload APIs called on non-HTTPS origin
recommendations.risk_mitigated: MITM credential interception on unencrypted connections

recommendations.title: Remove pre-filled credentials from login form
recommendations.description: Never persist email/password in sessionStorage for display. Fetch athlete name after auth, show readonly.

recommendations.title: Add value overflow guards to FIT encoder
recommendations.description: Assert power/HR/cadence fit within spec ranges before encoding
recommendations.risk_mitigated: Silent data corruption in edge cases

recommendations.title: Sanitize SVG color attributes
recommendations.description: Validate hex colors in profileShapes() with regex `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$`
recommendations.risk_mitigated: Future DOM injection if zone data becomes user-controlled

recommendations.title: Redact credentials from exception tracebacks
recommendations.description: Wrap password in custom class with safe `__repr__` method

architecture_notes.auth_model: Cookie-session with scrypt hashing. Public port requires session; loopback internal port (8223) trusted via socket, bypasses auth.
architecture_notes.secrets_handling: Garmin credentials transient (process-only during handshake). Telegram token from env. Upload tokens volatile (sessionStorage, cleared on tab close). Scrypt salt/hash in env file (0600).
architecture_notes.network_trust: Trust derived from accepting socket, not X-Forwarded-For header. Garmin egress via optional WARP proxy (socks5) to avoid IP rate-limiting.
areas_of_concern: XML parser no recursion depth limit
Credentials in browser storage (sessionStorage, not localStorage)

dependencies.risk: Loose version constraint allows automatic updates; unknown OAuth/credential handling changes

dependencies.risk: Custom fetch worker handles protocol details; minimal surface but unaudited

session_risk.impact: Sessions persist across password changes; no forced logout mechanism
session_risk.recommendation: Add GET /auth/logout that invalidates session cookie + revokes server-side session ID
